title: Gatineau cop cleared; Watchdog closes inquest into man's death
article: Quebec's independent police watchdog has closed the file on the death of a 69-year-old man in Gatineau last August.

The Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes and the provincial prosecutions office - the Directeur des poursuites criminelles et pénales - announced this past week that no charges would be filed against a Gatineau Police Service officer involved in an interaction with Laurent Levac just days before his death.

The BEI report said the officer went to a Gatineau apartment at about 8:30 p.m. on Aug. 21 following a 911 call about the 69-year-old man, who appeared confused and had gone to a neighbouring apartment for help in going to the bathroom. The officer noted the man seemed confused and weak and had difficulty moving, then escorted him to his own apartment and helped him to the bathroom.
Believing the man had lost the ability to live on his own, the officer suggested that he be transported to a hospital for care. The man refused, the BEI report said.

Estimating that it was a non-urgent situation, the police officer cancelled the call for paramedics, who had arrived at the building, but did not see the man. The officer remained with the man and made several attempts to contact relatives before leaving near 9:50 p.m. on the understanding that one of his relatives would come to the apartment after work and, in the interim, a building manager would monitor the man.

At about 10:10 p.m., though, paramedics were called back to the apartment by the man's daughter. The paramedics assessed the man, determined he was displaying symptoms of a stroke and immediately transported him to hospital.
He died five days later. An autopsy report said the death was caused by brain trauma.

Investigation revealed that on Aug. 19, two days before the police officer had responded to the 911 call, the man had fallen and hit his head against a wall. The prosecution office report said a pathologist determined that the injuries leading to the man's death compared to those from a fall.
Consequently, the prosecutions office said, there was no proof of a criminal act by the police officer. The results of the investigation were relayed to Levac's family, the report added.
The BEI report said it interviewed nine civilian witnesses, including paramedics, and analyzed reports by the officer who was in the apartment and another officer involved in the incident.
